verdict.line: You lose if you trade autos into his Leap Strike (Q) into Counter Strike (E) all-in; you win if you dodge that combo with E (Valor) and punish the long cooldowns it leaves behind.

brief.thesis: Jax holds the solo-kill edge because his Q (Leap Strike, 17/14/11/8/5s cd) into E (Counter Strike, 18/16/14/12/10s cd) is a forced all-in Riven can't out-trade in the open, but once those two cooldowns are spent he has no stun or mobility for a long stretch, which is exactly where Riven's Q-W-E rotation wins. That tension is why the data reads EVEN overall (48.5% win rate, 724 games) but defensive in shape — you're surviving his window to win yours.

theirWindow.when: Jax leaps in with Q off cooldown
theirWindow.what: He's walking into the Leap Strike (Q) into Counter Strike (E) combo OP.GG flags as his win condition. Don't stand and auto — his E dodges basic attacks and cuts AoE damage, so an auto or Ki Burst thrown in gets wasted. Dash away with E (Valor) the instant he commits.

yourWindow.when: His Q and E both just missed or landed
yourWindow.what: With Leap Strike and Counter Strike both on cooldown he has zero gap-close or stun for several seconds. Chain Q (Broken Wings) into W (Ki Burst) into E (Valor) for a full, unanswered trade.

start.why: Sustain through his early poke so you aren't forced to disengage before your W (Ki Burst) comes online at level 3.

boots.why: The measured pick (46.7% pick, 42.9% win rate) over Mercury's Treads — the cooldown this matchup is built around (Q/W/E rotation, not tenacity) matters more than magic resist against an all-AD kit.

core.why: The burst-and-shield spike that lets you win the trade right after his Q-E all-in has gone on cooldown.

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks through the extended trades this matchup is built around, then converts to healing once you're fully stacked — matching the defensive, whittle-him-down shape of the lane.

summoners.why: Flash is your clean answer to a committed Leap Strike (Q) into Counter Strike (E) all-in when E (Valor) alone isn't enough distance; Ignite punishes the all-in itself and closes out trades in a lane rated even on paper.

playing.title: Don't auto into Counter Strike
playing.detail: Jax's E (Counter Strike, 18/16/14/12/10s cd) dodges basic attacks and reduces AoE damage, so autos and Ki Burst thrown into it are wasted. Poke with Q (Broken Wings) instead or just back off with E (Valor) until it ends.

playing.title: Hold E for his Q leap
playing.detail: Jax's Q (Leap Strike, 17/14/11/8/5s cd) closes distance fast, especially at low levels. Use E (Valor) the instant he commits to deny the Q-E combo that gives him the solo-kill edge.

playing.title: Punish once his cooldowns are spent
playing.detail: After a failed or landed Q-E all-in, Jax has no stun or mobility for several seconds. That's your window to chain Q-W-E for a clean, unanswered trade.

playing.title: Track his Empower glow
playing.detail: Jax's W (Empower, 7/6/5/4/3s cd) buffs his next attack or leap and also damages nearby targets. A lit-up Empower is your cue an all-in is coming, not a free trade.

playing.title: Avoid greedy trades at levels 1-5
playing.detail: The lane is even overall but Jax holds the solo-kill advantage early. Don't commit to extended trades until your W (Ki Burst) and E (Valor) are both up to answer his leap.

playing.title: Poke, don't brawl
playing.detail: This matchup measures as defensive in shape. Win by chipping him down with Q and disengaging rather than standing in prolonged autos, where his R (Relentless Assault) attack-speed stacking punishes you.

playing.title: Force fights after Eclipse completes
playing.detail: Your burst through Q-W-E only outdamages his short trades once Eclipse is online. Look to commit to fights right after that spike, not before.

brief.patchCaveat: Build order, runes, summoners, and all win/pick rates above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG, with the Eclipse-Endless Hunger-Death's Dance core drawn from a very small sample (1 game) alongside two other listed paths; the ability mechanics, timing windows, and tactical reasoning are my own analysis, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Retreat with your abilities when Jax tries to close in with his Leap Strike (Q) – Counter Strike (E) combo. Harass Jax with your abilities, but keep an eye out for his (P) and Conqueror’s stacks.
